articleTitle: A Broadband SIW-Based Filtering Antenna for 5G mmWave Base Station Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A broadband mmWave base station filtering antenna based on substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW) structure is presented in this paper. The base station antenna consists of a pair of patches, two groups of L-shaped probes, and an SIW feeding structure. A wide band is obtained by etching the defected ground structure (DGS) and barbell slot on the SIW and loading the differential-fed L-shaped probe. Meanwhile, the filtering response is obtained by etching H-shaped slots on each radiating patch and adjusting the structure of SIW and probe. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 23.72-29.90 GHz and the realized gain is better than 6.3 dBi. The out-of-band suppression is greater than 12 dB.

articleTitle: A Lumped Elements Integrated Miniaturization Super-Wideband Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A lumped elements integrated miniaturization super-wideband antenna is proposed, which is fed by coplanar waveguide (CPW) that consists of feeding line, extended ground plane, three S-shaped-slot rectangle radiation patches and several integrated lumped elements. The three S-shaped-slot rectangle radiation patches are electromagnetically coupled by the balanced CPW feeding line. To enhance the bandwidth of the designed antenna, several lumped elements are integrated into the antenna. The designed antenna is modeled in CST. By co-simulation and optimizing using CST and ADS. A -10 dB fractional bandwidth of 169.5% can be achieved which ranges from 0.8 GHz-9.7 GHz. Moreover, the proposed antenna has good omnidirectional radiation patterns in the operating band.

articleTitle: Dead-zone-integrated Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons with Via-less Restrictions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a planar, single-layered antenna based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs). Slow waves can be converted into radiating waves by modulating the surface impedance of the SSPPs waveguide itself sinusoidally along its propagation direction. With the utilization of the single-sided defected square ring structure for SSPPs unit cell, the size of the proposed antenna is reduced, and the open- stopband effect which usually exists in symmetric structure can be eliminated. This antenna is designed for integrating in dead- zone area, in which only 0.3 mm width can be used for implementation. Numerical simulation results demonstrate a good performance of the design, which achieves a wide bandwidth from 54.3 GHz to 70 GHz, and it can scan continuously from the backward quadrant to the forward quadrant without gain reduction around the broadside direction.

articleTitle: Demonstration of IoT Sensors Powered by Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Ambient radio frequency (RF) powered Internet of Things (IoT) is a promising batteryless system for collecting environmental information for data exchange among devices. Ambient RF energy harvesting technology is most suitable for use in places that are hidden from light sources and are in difficult to reach places for battery replacement. In this paper, a demonstration of IoT sensors powered by ambient RF energy harvesting is presented. The system we have developed provides all key components from antenna, rectifier, power management unit (PMU), microcontroller unit (MCU) to sensing unit. In addition a novel 3-port antenna element for the systems is also described. The experimental results confirm that ambient RF signals can be regarded as an alternative to power supply in the next generation of wireless communications.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on a High-Order-Mode Dipole
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This research proposes a new circularly polarized (CP) antenna design utilizing a high-order-mode dipole. The dipole structure is compressed using a meander-line configuration. Two C-shape parasitic elements are proximity coupled by this dipole. The combination of the dipole and parasitic elements facilitates the generation of CP fields. The proposed design exhibits an overlapped bandwidth of 2.78% (2.48 – 2.55 GHz) for the -10-dB impedance and 3-dB axial ratio. Broadside radiation patterns are observed at the operating frequency. Leveraging the utilization of the high-order mode in the dipole, a maximum gain value of 9.71 dBic is obtained inside the overlapped passband.

articleTitle: Concept Proposal of Rear Feed Log-Periodic Film Antenna Using Microstrip Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a film antenna based on a log-periodic antenna, which has a wideband performance and unidirectional radiation. The proposed antenna is designed to operate from 0.7 to 6 GHz to cover 4G, 5G, and Wi-Fi bands. Generally, log-periodic antennas are fed from the tip of the antenna, and this is inconvenient for practical applications. The proposed antenna is fed from the rear of the antenna using microstrip lines printed on a polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film. The performance of the proposed antenna is examined by electromagnetic simulation. Antenna gains of 4 to 6 dB are obtained in a wide bandwidth from 0.7 to 6 GHz. The proposed antenna is cost effective and suitable for passive repeaters and Internet of Things (IoT) devices.

articleTitle: Permittivity extraction of multilayer coated bumper and bumper optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper showcases a method of extracting permittivity from multiple coated bumpers as well as optimizing the bumper thickness to improve radar transparency. The method follows an additive layer to extract the permittivity of each layer. The extraction method is verified with simulations. Bumper plastics coated with primer, base coat, and clear coat layers are fabricated and studied. The fabricated samples include four base coat layers, each consisting of different percentages of Aluminium powder. The extracted permittivity values of two independently fabricated clear coat samples are shown to be in good agreement which verifies the accuracy of the measurement and allows for better bumper thickness optimization.

articleTitle: On-Chassis Wideband Antenna for Vehicle Digital Television
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a new wideband antenna design utilized for vehicle digital television (DTV) application, where the antenna is integrated directly on a car chassis. It consists of a T-shape element, placed on a window opening of the car body. One part of the T-shape corresponds to a main radiation and the other part is for an additional radiation. The combination of the main and the additional ones creates wideband characteristic of the antenna, which covers the whole range of DTV application. The antenna can be installed at, for example, the quarter glass position of the car while maintaining it invisible from customers’ view.

articleTitle: Transmitarray Design of Dielectric Resonator Antennas Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This study explores a transmitarray design of dielectric resonator antennas operated in X-band (8-12 GHz). In our design, a 3×3 unit that includes the mutual coupling effect is employed to account for the coupling effect, with each sharing the same Floquet port. A two-head deep learning model based on the Res-Net architecture is developed to efficiently determine the phase value and transmission coefficient. With the height and diameter distribution being the inputs, the model successfully achieves a minimal mean squared error (MSE) loss of 0.2855 and a high Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.9954 on the test dataset. The effectiveness of the trained model is demonstrated through the optimization of a transmitarray using a sliding window approach, resulting in a synthesized window-transmitarray with superior gain performance compared to the conventional calculation methodologies.

articleTitle: Compact Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna with Isoflux Pattern for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Isoflux antenna is a kind of antenna with earth coverage radiation pattern, aiming to give equal power to different areas of the earth’s surface. Previous antennas with isoflux pattern are either bulky or lack multi-polarizations, making them unsuitable for small satellite applications. This paper presents a compact polarization reconfigurable antenna with isoflux pattern. The proposed antenna consists of a dielectric cylinder with a small cylinder cut off from the top, a circular patch antenna with four feeding ports. Through proper phasing of the four ports, the antenna can realize two orthogonal linear polarizations and two circular polarizations. With the use of the dielectric block above the circular radiating patch, the broadside radiation pattern can be enhanced. A 1 × 8 array is designed to validate the performance of the beam steering ability with small gain variation.

articleTitle: Phase Sensitivity Evaluation of Dual-Controlled Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Future 6G Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This study investigates the phase sensitivity of a dual-controlled reconfigurable intelligent surface (DC-RIS) when subjected to oblique illuminations. Unlike traditional RIS systems, the DC-RIS utilizes symmetry unit-cells and removes via-walls. Each component of the DC-RIS is regulated by a 2-bit varactor voltage at a maximum 10V. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the phase sensitivity differs between horizontally polarized (HP) and vertically polarized (VP) waves. While keeping the azimuth angle (α) constant at 45°, the phase sensitivity for HP decreases as the elevation angle (β) rises, while the phase sensitivity for VP experiences a rapid increase. For β=60°, the phase sensitivity is computed at 47.6°/bit for HP and 83.3°/bit for VP. Moreover, recommendations are proposed to address the issue of angular instability.

articleTitle: Grating-Lobe Suppressing Feed Technique for 2D Phased Array with Interpolating Excitation Elements in 300-GHz band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A 3×3 two-dimensional phased array was designed in 300-GHz band. Only corner 2×2 elements are fed from the feeding lines. Interpolating elements are located between the corner fed elements. The interpolating elements are excited by coupling circuits from both sides in intermediate phase. Although the spacing between the fed elements is larger than a wavelength in free space, grating lobes are suppressed by radiation from the interpolating elements and gain increases. The effect of the proposed technique on the phased array was confirmed by simulation in this work.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Slitted Waveguide Fed Mikaelian Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A near field focusing (NFF) planar gradient index (Mikaelian) lens antenna fed by a slitted waveguide is introduced. The structure is composed of a parallelepiped Mikaelian lens superstrate positioned on top of a one-dimensional continuous source provided by a rectangular waveguide leaky-wave antenna (LWA). The design of the lens superstrate by ray tracing is discussed and the focusing performance of the combined feed and lens is then verified by full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: An Exploratory Study for the Design of Transcutaneous Antennas for High Data-rate Full-duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Here we present a study on antenna designs aimed at supporting low energy and ultimately very high data-rate (100 Mb/s to Gb/s) transcutaneous wireless links. Such links can enable implantable biosensors as well as multi electrode sensing and stimulation arrays for electromyography (EMG) and functional electrical stimulation (FES) and the associated microelectronics. Thus, the design and performance of a dihedral reflector backed miniaturized dipole antenna (DADR) is examined as a proof of concept for transdermal applications and compared with a common microstrip patch antenna approach for carrier frequencies ≤ 10 GHz. For this study the dielectric properties of animal tissue samples were measured and data representing the frequency dependent losses are modelled in a simulation environment. A performance comparison involving the tissue models is conducted between the proposed DADR and conventional microstrip antenna. The study is conducted by utilising a high operating frequency with a view to enable significantly enhanced data rates as necessary for multi-electrode arrays featuring tens to thousands of individual signals. The proposed transcutaneous reflector-dipole antenna pair achieved an end-to-end propagation loss of 7.53 dB (17.66% power transfer ratio) at 8.4 GHz through a 3 mm thick tissue sample. By comparison, a microstrip-to-microstrip antenna propagation loss was 11.5 dB (7% power transfer ratio). This is an important evaluation for both link-budget calculations and subsequent design of minimum implant electronics and transceiver power dissipation, and for specific absorption ratio (SAR) purposes.

articleTitle: Efficient Methods to Enhance the Bandwidths of Transmitarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper introduces two efficient methods to enhance the bandwidths of transmitarray antennas. For the transmitarray antenna based on resonant unit cells, two unit cells based on polarization-rotation structures are proposed to offer a 2-bit transmission phase, where the resizing unit cell is avoided to widen the bandwidth. For the lens antenna based on dielectric stubs, four unit cells are selected to offer a 2-bit transmission phase as well, to broaden the bandwidth, the effects of the oblique incidences are considered and eliminated. For the first transmitarray antenna using the proposed method, the measured 1- and 3-dB gain bandwidth is 28.0 - 37.5 GHz (29.5%) and 25.1 - 39.1 GHz (43.7%), respectively. For the second lens antenna using the corresponding proposed method, the measured 1-dB gain bandwidth is 24.8 – 30 GHz (18.9%). The proposed two methods are generalized and is also feasible for reflectarray antennas and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave On-Chip Aperture-Coupled Patch Antennas Using Hot-Via Street Option in a GaAs Integrated Passive Device Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: On-chip aperture-coupled patch antennas are designed and fabricated using a GaAs integrated passive device (IPD) process with hot-via street (HVST) option. The HVST option enables partial removal of the back-side metal and therefore the creation of rectangular patches. Two aperture-coupled patch antennas are designed at 40 GHz and 80 GHz, respectively. Measurement results show that greatest return loss occurs near the frequency of design for each antenna. Simulated antenna gains are 3.3 dBi and 4.6 dBi for the 40-GHz and 80-GHz antennas, respectively. The results validate the idea of using HVST option to implement aperture-coupled patch antennas.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Cylindrical Dielectric Resonant Antenna for Tri-band Wi-Fi Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A tri-band dual-polarized cylindrical dielectric resonant antenna is proposed for WiFi applications. The antenna is fed with planar structures, operating in three frequency bands: 2.4-2.5 GHz, 5.17-5.25 GHz, and 5.73-5.835 GHz. Each frequency band has two modes: horizontal and vertical polarized modes, with isolation higher than 23 dB between them. All modes have desirable omnidirectional radiation fields with low cross polarization. The peak gain of this omnidirectional antenna is higher than 0.5 dBi for all modes. This antenna can be used in WiFi routers to replace four traditional monopole antennas.

articleTitle: Foldable Dual Linear Polarized Dipole L band Antenna Using Polyimide and Gamma Match
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A foldable dual linear polarized antenna with gamma match at L band is presented. Two crossed dipoles are fed by two feed networks with gamma match to achieve the two polarizations. Since the gamma match uses the ground in the center of the radiator, it is relatively easy to extend the conventional single polarization to dual polarization. The feed networks are printed on two sides of a rigid PTFE substrate, while the radiators are printed on one side of flexible copper cladded polyimide substrate. Taking advantage of feed network’s planar configuration and the use of flexible substrate, the dualpolarized antenna can be folded with low profile. Thus the proposed dual polarized dipole antenna is a good candidate for L-band space applications where the antenna must be stowable and deployable.

articleTitle: A Nonradiative Dielectric Waveguide Based Wideband Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper introduces the design of a reflectarray antenna (RA) based on a nonradiative dielectric (NRD) waveguide. The proposed design achieves wideband performance by eliminating the need for traditional resonant components. Unstable reflection coefficient of the element under oblique incidence is investigated and addresses through a specific feed configuration. The 16×16 RA prototype exhibits a verified capability for maximum collimation beam angles up to 60°, accompanied by a gain variation of under 1.5 dB within the frequency range of 9.5 GHz to 11.5 GHz, with relative low beam squint.

articleTitle: Estimation of Phased Array Deformation Using Two Received Noisy Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A method is presented to estimate the shape of a deformed uniform linear array (ULA) using two received signals. The two signals can be noiseless ir contaminated with noise, which is of practical importance when deformation must be estimated using signals from a distance away from the array. Two sources with known angle of arrival (AOA) are used to estimate the distance and the angle of the deformed element with respect to the non-deformed element. The proposed estimation technique is applied to a deformed array with eight elements, and parametric studies of estimation performance are provided.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of an Extended Pseudo-Scale Model for Air-Brackish Two-Layer Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: To reduce the experimental cost of underwater locating, a pseudo-scale model was proposed, which could be applied to the air-sea water two-layer problem, but not to the air-brackish water two-layer problem. In this paper, we attempt to apply an extended pseudo-scale model to measure the electromagnetic field distribution in the air-brackish water two-layer problem in the laboratory. To experimentally confirm the validity of this model, we assume an electrically infinitesimal dipole antenna in the water region for the diver locating problem near the water surface using electromagnetic waves, and compare the electric field distribution obtained by numerical simulation using the FDTD method for the original problem with the measured received power distribution for the extended pseudo-scale model. Taking into account the scale factor, we can confirm that the difference between these distributions is small.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized MACKEY with Broader Bandwidth by Changing Antenna Plate Angle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A metasurface-inspired antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY), which operates in free space and on a metal plate, was investigated in this study. This study presents analytical results of the MACKEY C3P1X- type, which is a conventional circularly polarized MACKEY C3P1type with a wider bandwidth by modifying the antenna plate.

articleTitle: Development of Millimeter-Wave Reconfigurable Reflect-Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this work, we report the recent development of millimeter-wave reconfigurable reflect-array. By properly loading PIN diodes into reflective unit cells, 1-bit and 2-bit phase shifting can be achieved, providing a cost-efficient solution to beam steering antennas at millimeter-wave frequencies. In particular, a single-polarized 2-bit reflect-array of 1300 cells and a broadband dual-polarized 1-bit reflect-array of 400 cells are realized at Ka-band, showing a good agreement between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Adaptive Switchable FSS Design with High Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this article, an ultra-wideband adaptive switchable FSS with high selectivity is proposed. The passive cell has steep sidebands, and ultra-wide passband. PIN diodes are loaded to switch pass-stop state, and the effect of parasitic capacitance is analyzed and optimized. Fast adaptive control system is designed to control the switchable FSS, and principal prototype is manufactured. In PASS state, the measured −3 dB passband is from 1.92 to 12 GHz, and the transition bandwidth from −3 dB to −20 dB is only 106 MHz. |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>| in STOP state is less than −5 dB from 1 to 18 GHz. The average adaptive switching time is less than 25 ms.

articleTitle: Aperture-Shared Reflectarray Antenna for Sub-6 GHz and Mm-Wave Dual-Band Dual Circular Polarization Independent Beam-Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This article presents an aperture-shared reflectarray supporting Sub-6 GHz and millimeter-wave (mm-wave) dual-band dual circular polarization independent beam-shaping. A square patch is implemented in the top layer working at Sub-6 GHz. The Sub-6 GHz patch connects to a branch line coupler. The LHCP/RHCP phases is independently manipulated by the phase delay lines connecting to the coupler. As for the mm-wave dual CP independent beam shaping, two different cells are implemented on the aperture and integrated with the patch antenna. By adjusting the size and properly rotating the angle of the UC, the LHCP/RHCP components can be independently manipulated. A reflectarray antenna operating at Sub-6 GHz and 30 GHz with dual CP decoupled beams is designed for verification.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Transmit-Receive Horn Antenna Based on a Nonreciprocal Metasurface with Embedded Magnetic Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Many simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) antenna systems require a ferrite circulator to separate transmitted and received signals. However, conventional ferrite circulators exhibit drawbacks, such as large size and limited isolation. This paper introduces an X-band STAR antenna consisting of a horn antenna integrated with a novel passive metasurface that exhibits Faraday rotation. The metasurface is composed of a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) wafer with embedded neodymium magnets that are held together by dielectric substrates. The substrates provide impedance matching and extend the operational bandwidth. The metasurface, with embedded magnets, is mounted to the horn’s aperture. The proposed antenna is described in detail, including its operating principle, design, and simulated performance.

articleTitle: A Yagi-Uda Antenna Implemented with Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a Yagi-Uda antenna implemented with solar cells. An ultra-low-profile copper indium gallium selenide (CIGS)-based solar cell was used as a driver, and a slot was cut in the driver to feed the antenna. A CIGS solar-cell-based reflector and director were added to form a Yagi-Uda antenna. The spacing between the reflector, driver, and director were minimized to increase the solar-cell form factor. A coaxial-to-microstrip line transitiontype feeding structure was used for wideband impedance matching. Three RF decoupler circuits were designed for the driver, reflector, and director so that the antenna and solar cell could function independently. The antenna has overall dimensions of 0.71 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> × 0.61 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> × 0.006 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> at 3.2 GHz, an impedance bandwidth of 56.74%, and a maximum gain of 5.67 dBi within the impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: 2D Beam-Steerable Array Antennas for 5G Antenna-in-Package Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this research, a compact dual-polarized (DP) dielectric cavity antenna is presented for wide-angle two dimensional (2D) scanning phased arrays, operating in the 5G n261 band. The design utilizes low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology, advantageous for scalability at millimeter-wave (mmW) frequencies. The antenna consists of a dielectric cavity fed by a cross-shaped slot, with a metasurface layer atop the cavity to improve active impedance-matching to air. Designed in a compact multilayer LTCC substrate, the antenna element is examined in an infinite array setting and characterized through an 8 × 8 array architecture, comprising 2 × 2 subarray tiles. Optimized for the n261 band (27.5-28.35 GHz), the design achieves an active reflection coefficient |Γ| ≤ −10 dB within the ±60° scan range. The array exhibits a scan loss between 2.9 dB to 3.8 dB in the H-, D-, and V-planes for both polarizations.

articleTitle: Study on Miniaturized, Circularly Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna Using DGS at S-band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The design and fabrication of a miniaturized, circularly polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna (MPA) for wireless and small satellite applications at S-band is reported in this paper. The Defected Ground Structure (DGS) technique is applied in a normal circular polarization MPA to create a degree of miniaturization. The results showed that the miniaturized antenna has an operation frequency of around 2.47 GHz while having the same size as the original antenna working at 3.1 GHz, it means that it is a miniaturization efficiency of 21% has been reached. The measured gain is about 1 dBi at 2.47 GHz. Additionally, the AR is below 3 dB at this operation frequency, it indicates that the quality of circular polarization has been maintained. This antenna design is promising when applied in compact wireless devices, as well as small satellites applications.

articleTitle: A MIMO antenna design with closed slot for Wi-Fi 6E Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A MIMO antenna design with closed slot for Wi-Fi 6E frequency band has been presented. This paper is designed on the upper edge of the metal frame of the notebook computer screen, by exciting the mode of the closed slot to achieve operation in Wi-Fi 6E band, and use the dual slot to achieve the effect of MIMO. Two closed slots with dimensions of 41 x 3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are placed at 13.5 mm and 8.5 mm on the upper left edge of the 200 x 300 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> screen metal plate. The distance between the two closed slots is 20 mm. The feed-in device is placed above the closed slot and consists of a 44 x 6 x 0.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> FR4 board (ɛr=4.4) and two 1 x 3.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> feeds. The (2400-2500 /5150-7125 MHz) dual modes are excited by the feed-source coupling closed slot. Using the feature of high isolation of the slot, the distance between the dual radiation source elements can be pulled closer. In terms of simulation and measured, the S11 parameters are all below -6dB, and the isolation is below -15dB, which has good radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: A Compact Multiband Monopole Antenna for Wi-Fi Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact multiband monopole antenna designed for Wi-Fi applications, covering frequency bands including the 2.4GHz band, 3.5GHz band (sub-6G), 5GHz band, and 6GHz band. These frequency bands encompass both previous standards such as 802.11x and the latest 802.11ax and 802.11be, corresponding to Wi-Fi 6/6e and Wi-Fi 7. The antenna is constructed from a low-cost two-layer FR-4 PCB with dimensions of 30 x 10 x 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The antenna features four resonant frequencies at 2.45GHz, 3.56GHz, 5.52GHz, and 6.41GHz, enabling the desired bandwidth. Furthermore, the antenna demonstrates excellent performance at these resonant frequencies, all exhibiting the expected omni-directional radiation patterns, with gains of 1.71dBi, 2.06dBi, 4.25dBi, and 4.11dBi, respectively. The compact multiband monopole antenna is highly suitable for wireless routers, IoT devices, and various applications in the context of Wi-Fi 7 in the future.

articleTitle: Design of Optically Transparent Metasurface for Microwave Wireless Power Transmission with a Nondiffractive Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: An optically transparent reflective metasurface utilizing indium tin oxide (ITO) is proposed for applications in microwave wireless power transmission (MWPT). The sub-wavelength element achieved a peak return loss within 1.5dB and phase variation exceeding 360° at a frequency of 5.8GHz. An optically transparent single-layer metasurface is composed of 53×53 elements, which is able to achieve a nondiffractive beam of 2m in simulation, with radiated power attenuation of less than 5.5dB. Furthermore, the deflection of nondiffractive zero-order Bessel beams by 10° +z-axis has been attained, with an emission efficiency of 75.21% at 1500mm.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Decoupled Circular Polarization Microstrip Antennas Using Metal Pins
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a radiation pattern decoupling (RPD) method using metal pins for circular polarization microstrip antennas (CPMAs). The loaded metal pin couples an extra anti-phase current that effectively cancels out the original coupled current on the coupled patch. This cancellation effect allows the antenna to obtain RPD characteristic. To verify the RPD method, a 1×2 CPMA array is designed at 3.6 GHz. It is important to note that the radiation patterns of the decoupled antennas all along the broadside direction. This characteristic is defined as the RPD.

articleTitle: A Compact Orthogonal-Mode Decoupling Network for Metal-Rimmed MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A high-isolated dual-antenna pair based on orthogonal-mode excitations is presented for mainstream metalrimmed smartphones in this article. The decoupling of the dualantenna pair can be achieved by integrating two antenna units in the same radiator and feeding it with a modified directional coupler. The antenna will excite the orthogonal dipole and monopole modes when two external ports are fed separately. With this decoupling scheme, the dual-antenna pair shows an isolation of more than 15 dB, and the reflection coefficients are below -8 dB in 3.4-3.6 GHz. In addition, we optimize the size of the feeding coupler to make the overall structure smaller, which is in line with the trend of antenna miniaturization.

articleTitle: Compact and easy antenna with reflector for 2.4-GHz applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Antennas for IoT terminals need to have a compact design to permit mobility and must be easy to manufacture to ensure high productivity and low cost. It is also desirable to reduce the influence of metals near the antenna, i.e., to make it unidirectional to enable ease of installation. The 'COSY' antenna was developed to meet these three requirements. It consists of a radiator and a reflector. The radiator has a simple configuration that consists of a plate element and a linear element and operates at the desired frequency by coupling with a reflector. This configuration suppresses any reduction in radiation resistance. The conventional type has a two-component configuration comprising a copper foil on FR-4 substrate for the radiator and a thin copper plate for the reflector. This paper first considers a simpler integrated model in which the radiator and reflector are formed from copper foil on both sides of a FR-4 board. Terminal antennas need to achieve a broadband configuration in addition to being compact in size. Therefore, after this section, a broadband model using dual-resonant matching with a parasitic element will be discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Analysis of TV and/or Radio Broadcasting Transmitting Tower Station located nearby Observation Deck
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper started with a proposal for Busan's development plan, aiming to build an observation deck that would become a landmark in Busan, Korea at the position of the Hwangryeong mountain observatory tower. Given the proximity of transmission stations tower such as KBS, MBC, and KNN broadcasting station within approximately 100 meters of the Hwangryeong Mountain observatory tower, this paper aims to present the content and results of an electromagnetic environment analysis conducted as part of a study to assess the intensity, wave direction, and counterplan for potential electromagnetic interference, when a observation deck will be constructed at the location of the Hwangryeong Mountain observatory tower.

articleTitle: Research and Development of Yagi-Uda antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Yagi-Uda antenna was first reported by Shintaro Uda in December 1925 in the Journal of the Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan under the title "On the wireless beam of short electric waves", and subsequently English paper entitled "Projector of the sharpest beam of electric waves" was published by Yagi and Uda in the Proceedings of Imperial Academy Japan in 1926. Furthermore, 11 papers entitled "On the wireless beam of short electric waves" were published by Uda on detailed experiments regarding the Yagi-Uda antenna. Based on these papers, an overview of the principle and development of the Yagi-Uda antenna is presented. Long-distance communication experiments in the UHF band (600MHz), as well as the history of experiments and practical applications in the VHF band (65MHz, 53MHz, 38MHz) using this antenna and the developed transceiver are described. An overview of the IEEE Milestone dedicated to the invention of this antenna in 1995, which was the first Milestone in the Asia-Oceania region, is also presented.

articleTitle: Simple Measurement Method for Reflectarray Using Monostatic-Bistatic Equivalence Theorem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Reflectarray has gained attention to reduce the coverage holes in 5G. Reflectarray is evaluated by the bistatic radar cross section (RCS) measurements. However, bistatic RCS measurements are complicated as compared to monostatic RCS measurement. This paper presents the monostatic-bistatic equivalent theorem (MBET) to estimate bistatic scattering fields of reflectarray. By using the MBET, the bistatic RCS pattern of reflectarray can be predicted by the simple measurement of the monostatic RCS. The effectiveness of the MBET is demonstrated for the reflectarray with tilt beam and dual beam in the simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Wideband Patch Array Antenna with Parallel Connected Series-Fed Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this paper, a millimeter wide-band patch array antenna with parallel connected series-fed network is proposed. Firstly, based on the parallel feed, two 1×2 microstrip array antennas with the working center frequency of 61 and 63 GHz were designed, with a bandwidth of 1.01% and 1.11 %, respectively. Then in order to expand the working bandwidth of the proposed array antenna, the two array antennas were combined. Meanwhile, a hybrid mode of series and parallel feeding was adopted to design a 2×2 patch array antenna to save space of the feed network and facilitate adjustment of the array antenna. Ultimately, the proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 60.3-64 GHz (5.95 %), with a total gain of up to 11.3 dBi within the array antenna's working band.

articleTitle: A Triangular Dual-Band Patch Antenna with Harmonic Frequencies Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Microstrip patch antennas with various shapes and performances are often used due to their inheritance characteristics such as low-profile, ease of installation, low cost, and capability for multi-band operation. However, due to its other characteristic in generating harmonic frequencies, it is necessary to give more attention to these frequencies to avoid interfering with the desired ones. This paper presents the design and characterization of a triangular dual-band patch antenna with arc slot insertions for harmonic frequency suppression. The proposed antenna is intended to work at the frequencies of 0.91 GHz and 2.45 GHz for radio telemetry communication applications. It is designed on a 1.575 mm thick FR-4 epoxy dielectric substrate with a relative permittivity of 4.3 and dimensions of 140 mm × 120 mm. The result shows that by insertion of arc slots, the suppression of second, third and fifth frequencies reaches up to 0.51 dB, 2.55 dB and 3.35 dB respectively. Whereas, the coefficient reflection of the dual-band is maintained less than -10 dB.

articleTitle: PIN Diode-Based Switchable Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna for GPS L1 Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper explores the switchable polarization capability of microstrip patch antenna by utilizing PIN diode to examine how it is influenced by the polarization mismatch. The polarization of electromagnetic waves radiated by the antenna may experience depolarization during propagation, leading to polarization loss factor (PLF) and decreasing received power intensity. The proposed switchable polarized microstrip patch antenna, which is designed to address the depolarization issue for Global Positioning System (GPS) L1 application, is primarily developed on an RT/Duroid 5880 dielectric substrate. The realized microstrip patch antenna demonstrates the capability to switch between circular and linear polarizations using four PIN diodes.

articleTitle: Wideband Low-Sidelobe Circularly Polarized Array Using Sequential Subarray Rotation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This work presents a wideband low-sidelobe 2×10 circularly polarized helix antenna array using sequential subarray rotation. To avoid grating lobes in uniformly distributed sequential rotation arrays, adjacent subarrays are rotated by 180°. A wideband low-sidelobe array is designed. Each subarray consists of four sequentially rotated helix elements for high-purity circular polarization. A 3-dB hybrid coupler provides wideband 90° phase difference. Taylor-distributed excited coefficient is implemented in feed network to suppress sidelobe. Simulated results show that the sidelobe level on horizontal plane is below -22 dB in 6-7.5 GHz, while the axial ratio is lower than 1.7 dB.

articleTitle: Radiation-Scattering-Integrated Design of A Circularly Polarized Metantenna with Low Radar Cross-Section
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A circularly polarized metantenna with low radar cross-section characteristics is presented. A spindle-shaped microstrip patch, along with two "V"-shaped metal strips acts as both the antenna radiator and the unit cell of polarization conversion metasurface. The antenna elements can achieve both excellent radiation and scattering performance simultaneously when excited by the sequentially rotated feeding. Simulated results show that the band of |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < −10 dB for all ports covers from 8.5 to 9.7 GHz with a maximum gain of 12 dBi at 8.6 GHz. The design reduces the monostatic radar cross section by 10 dB from 7.1 to 9.3 GHz.

articleTitle: An Integrated Imaging Sensing and MMW Communication System with Universal Software Radio Peripheral
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Utilizing millimeter-wave (MMW) communication systems for inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging perception represents an innovative application in achieving integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). In this work, we have implemented an ISAC system by utilizing the universal software radio peripheral (USRP). The system provides a 100 MHz communication signal bandwidth and consists of an MMW base station transmitter for downlink communication signals and a perception receiver for capturing target reflection signals. Target perception and imaging are achieved through the extraction and processing of the terminal's channel state information (CSI). Experimental measurements validate the reliability of the imaging system.

articleTitle: D-band Antenna Module Combining a FOWLP Antenna-in-Packaging and GRIN Lens featuring Flat-top Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this work, we present a D-band antenna module with a flat-top radiation pattern for mm-wave wireless systems. The module includes a perforated low- temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCC) Gradient-Index (GRIN) lens and a uniform planar array (UPA) of silicon resonator antennas integrated with active RFIC in Fan-out wafer level packaging (FOWLP). The FOWLP antenna-in-packaging (AiP) comprises 16 silicon resonator antennas fed by four 8 Multiplier chains in 28-nm FDSOI CMOS. The peaked realized gain of the AiP is 14.8 dBi and the Multiplier operation band is from 152.8 GHz to 165.8 GHz. The LTCC-based GRIN Lens is designed to convert the sharp beam of the AiP to the desired flat-top radiation pattern. The simulation and primary measurement results validate the performance of the proposed antenna module.

articleTitle: A study on parallel-arranged leaky wave antenna with dielectric superstrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this report, a parallel-arranged leaky wave antenna with dielectric superstrate is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a ground plane, a substrate layer, and a superstrate layer. Half of the substrate layer is filled with dielectric, and the other half is filled with air to create a quasi-cutoff region. We parallelly arranged three types of elements with different effective relative permittivity in substrate layer along the E-plane direction. Each element has a different beam direction, and by changing the feeding port, the beam direction can be controlled. The influence of parallel LWADS configuration on the radiation pattern was examined, and its suitability as a beam switching antenna was studied.

articleTitle: A Low-SAR Frame-Antenna for Mobile Phone Based on Tangential Fields Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A low specific absorption rate (SAR) frame antenna for smartphone is proposed based on the tangential fields cancellation. The proposed antenna contains a T-shaped feeding, a modified folded dipole and loaded inductors, which are used to cancel tangential electric field by introducing reverse current. The measured -6dB bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 335MHz from 3.3GHz-3.6GHz. The measured total efficiency ranges from 62% to 85%. The measured normalized maximum 10g peak spatial-average SAR is 1.09W/kg. The SARs in different reference planes also have similar magnitudes and distribution and can all be kept at a low level.

articleTitle: Lorentz Dispersive Metamaterial for Single-mode Dual-band Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper explores the attributes of the Lorentz model dispersive material, Lorentz-dispersive material in short, and its application in antenna design. Initially, the Lorentz model and its physical interpretation will be elucidated. Subsequently, the material with Lorentz dispersive permittivity and permeability will be used for antenna designs. Owing to the unique dispersive characteristics of permittivity and permeability, leading to a higher refractive index at lower frequencies and a lower refractive index at higher frequencies, the wavelength within the Lorentz-dispersive material can remain consistent across two distinct frequencies. For the application, the conventional rectangular patch antenna is designed employing Lorentz-dispersive material and metamaterial. Leveraging the consistent wavelength within the Lorentz-dispersive property at two specific frequencies, the patch can maintain an identical electrical size across two different frequencies. This enables the TM10 (or TM01) mode to operate simultaneously at both frequencies. The outcomes further demonstrate that an n-mode antenna can achieve operation at 2n frequencies by employing appropriately chosen Lorentz-dispersive metamaterial as a substrate.

articleTitle: An omnidirectional antenna for CPE device application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: We use magnetic current and electric current to form desired omni-directional radiation factor owing to the current phase difference is 90 degrees. In this paper, the radiation elements form as a circle to control the phase difference, adopting three elements with simple structures are placed at specific angles each other to generate omnidirectional far-field in XY-plane. The overall size that we proposed design is 44.40(L) x 39.90(W) mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to apply in CPE device. The antenna is fabricated on FR4 substrate with thickness of 0.8mm with S11 <= -10 dB impedance matching level. In the future work, it can apply to MIMO system with high isolation at close distance.

articleTitle: A 0.3-6 GHz Ultra-Wideband Vivaldi Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-wideband Vivaldi array antenna. The Vivaldi antenna in the infinite array is designed based on the periodic boundary, whose operating bandwidth is range 0.27-6.18 GHz. When an infinite array is reduced to a finite array, the performance of the array antenna elements will be significantly reduced due to the truncation effect. This paper proposes to place metal plates on both sides of the array to minimize the truncation effect. In the proposed 1 × 12 array antenna, the reflection coefficient of the array elements is less than -10 dB in the range of 0.3-6.17 GHz and the gain of the array antenna is ranging from 5.54 to 22.4 dBi. The array antenna has small side lobes on the E-plane.

articleTitle: Negative Capacitor and Inductor with Loss Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The realization of negative capacitor and inductor promise superior performance to the conventional integrated circuit composed of positive capacitor and inductor. In practical consideration, it is necessary for the losses of the proposed negative capacitor and inductor to be investigated. In this study, we try to demonstrate the loss issue of the negative capacitor and inductor, aiming to exhibit the performance of negative capacitor and inductor with different levels of losses and provide a guideline of the practical circuit design with negative elements.

articleTitle: Flexible and Conformal Antennas Based on Corrugated Copper Clad Polyimide Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Lightweight flexible antennas based on single-layer and multilayer corrugated copper clad polyimide films are presented. The single-layer corrugated patch antenna (SLCPA) comprises a patch radiator with semicircular-shaped corrugations. In the multilayer corrugated patch antenna (MLCPA) an additional corrugated patch is added to the SLCPA to increase the bandwidth while maintaining good conforming properties. Both antennas are designed for the L band and tested for the flat case as well as conformed to a cylinder with radius of 160 mm, 80 mm, 40 mm, and 20 mm. The MLCPA has a bandwidth of 1.198–1.33 GHz (10.42%), and the gain varies from 5.78 dBi to 8.67 dBi for different cases of conforming to a cylinder.

articleTitle: Study of Dual-Band Horn Antennas for Offset Parabolic Reflector Antenna in 12- and 21-GHz- Band Satellite Broadcasting Reception
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The 12-GHz band (11.7 to 12.75 GHz) is used for satellite broadcasting of high-definition television and ultra- high-definition television in Japan. Moreover, the 21-GHz band (21.4 to 22.0 GHz) has been allocated to satellite broadcasting in Europe, Africa, and Asia Pacific. The BSAT-4a satellite has not only 12-GHz-band transponders but also 21-GHz-band transponders for future broadcasting services. To receive the services using these two frequency bands with a single antenna, we have studied a receiving antenna composed of an offset parabolic reflector and a 12- and 21-GHz dual-band feed horn antenna. In this study, we designed two types of dual-band horn antenna and evaluated the performance of the reflector antenna configuration. Simulation results showed that an aperture efficiency of more than 70% was obtained in both bands.

articleTitle: Design of Switchable Dual-Axis Monopulse Array Antenna With Wide Beam-Steering Functionality Employing Tri-State SPDT Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a switchable dual-axis monopulse antenna with wide beam-steering functionality. The proposed antenna consists of four linearly polarized microstrip antennas, a magic-T, a phase-shift-keying (PSK) modulator, and two tri-state single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switches. The SPDT switches control the beam steering in three different conditions. According to the amplitude ratio of magic-T's two input signals, the phase difference of the patches changes so that the beam tilts. The proposed antenna employs a PSK modulator to achieve a wide range of beam steering among ±20°.

articleTitle: Steering Radiated Beam of a Helical Antenna Using Plasma Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to improve the steering capabilities of helical antennas with plasma reflectors. The proposed method is based on the implementation of two half-cup plasma reflectors. The study thoroughly examines the influence the dimensions of the second reflector on the radiation characteristics of the antenna. The results of fullwave electromagnetic simulations demonstrates the potential of the proposed method for electronic beam steering, achieving a remarkable steering of up to ±27 degrees. The strategic placement of the plasma reflectors on two sides of the helical antenna showcases promising steering capabilities. However, optimizing performance requires a delicate balance in reflector dimensions, crucial especially for maintaining circular polarization. Notably, this antenna design leverages the inherent controllability of the plasma reflectors, enabling selective activation and electrical adjustments in dimensions and positions.

articleTitle: Recent Progress in Circularly Polarized Meta-antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The recent progress in circularly polarized (CP) meta-antennas is discussed. The following topics are described: beam steering for a bent meta-line array antenna, gain enhancement for a left-hand CP wave using a conducting patch printed within a meta-loop antenna, a technique for rejecting interference signals using a null field created within a meta-spiral antenna, and realization of a balanced gain for the left-and right-hand CP waves radiated from a meta-curl antenna.

articleTitle: Standing Wave Dual-Band Substrate Integrated Waveguide Slotted Array Antenna for mmWave Automotive Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The design of a dual-band Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) slotted array antenna for millimeter-wave (mmWave) automotive radar application is presented. A single feed with a taper coplanar waveguide (CPW)-to-SIW transition excites the antenna. To generate a dual-band, rectangular slots of 60 and 77 GHz are etched on each side of the array. The proposed antenna works as a directional antenna at 60 GHz and an omnidirectional antenna at 77 GHz. With a single feed, the proposed dual-band antenna of 60 GHz and 77 GHz exhibit 13.5 and 15 dBi gain, respectively, and efficiency of 65% and 65.5%, respectively. Also, each band of the dual-band is wide, around 3.38 GHz (5.6%) and 3.37 GHz (4.37%), respectively.

articleTitle: Self-decoupled U-slot Patch Antenna based on Field Valleys Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A self-decoupled U-slot patch antenna based on field valleys distribution is proposed for multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) applications. This antenna has two field valleys of the current distribution along the E plane. Due to the presence of field valleys, decoupling of the E-plane array can be effectively obtained. The asymmetry in the locations of the field valleys gives rise to three different array orientations. Based on this self-decoupled antenna, high-isolation E-plane arrays can be realized.

articleTitle: Study of Single Point-Feed Wi-Fi 2GHz/5GHz Band Antenna Using MACKEY A-Shaped Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: MACKEY (Meta-surface inspired Antenna Chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory) has been proposed as a functional compact antenna that is not affected by surrounding metals. MACKEY T (Triple Grids Type) has also been proposed for Wi-Fi 2GHz and Wi-Fi 5GHz bands. In this report, we present the analysis results of the MACKEY A (Asymmetry Type), which is a modification of the conventional T-type for the shared use of Wi-Fi 2GHz and Wi-Fi 5GHz bands.

articleTitle: 2-bit Intelligent Reflection Surface Enhances Urban Wireless Communications: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Intelligent Reflective Surfaces (IRS) have emerged as a promising technology for future wireless communication, Due to system complexity constraints, most IRS implementations have adopted 1-bit reconfigurable schemes, lacking test results in outdoor real communication environments. This paper introduces a novel 2-bit phase reconfigurable IRS design method, where each Radio Frequency (RF) unit is independently controlled, allowing arbitrary switching between 4 different phase states to adapt to the varying complexities of communication environments. Furthermore, the comparative transmission experiments in an outdoor far-field environment have been implemented. The experimental results demonstrate that deploying the IRS can significantly enhance the signal reception power for blind zone users in urban settings. Compared to a metal plate, our IRS prototype exhibits exceptional beam control flexibility, showcasing a promising avenue for urban wireless enhancement.

articleTitle: Full-Vectorial Bidirectional Beam Propagation Method For Efficient Numerical Analysis of THz NRD Guide Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a full-vectorial finite-element 3D bidirectional beam propagation method (FVFE-3DBiBPM) for numerical analysis of THz dielectric waveguide components sandwiched by metal parallel plates. In order to consider conductor loss of parallel metal plates and reduce computational cost, we study on the FVFE-BiBPM using an impedance boundary condition (IBC). As a numerical example, we analyze propagation behavior of THz wave in a nonradiative dielectric waveguide (NRD guide) with an air-gap, and the numerical example shows the validity of the FVFE-BiBPM with the IBC.

articleTitle: Design of a Circularly Polarized Dipole Antenna with Twisted Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The paper presents a circularly polarized dipole antenna with twisted elements. By twisting the flat plate elements, the current flow from the feeding point toward the edge of the elements is effectively directed to the longitudinal direction of the elements. As a result, circular polarization with the axial ratio below 3 dB is observed from 5.8 GHz to 7.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysing a Horn Antenna at 220–330 GHz Using Simulations and Near-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Wireless communications at sub-THz frequencies require high-gain antennas for practical link distances and increase the complexity of design and testing. This work investigates the operation of a pyramidal horn antenna operating at 220–330 GHz. The antenna is studied using both electromagnetic (EM) simulations and near-field measurements with a planar scanner. The obtained results are in good agreement regarding the frequency response and radiation pattern properties, which validates the experimental setup used for measurements at frequencies above 300 GHz.

articleTitle: Scattering Beam Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A circularly polarized antenna array with reconfigurable scattering patterns is proposed. The proposed antenna unit integrates four p-i-n diodes, enabling the unit to achieve two operational states by tuning the states of these diodes. Both states of the unit exhibit a 180° reflection phase difference but show similar radiation characteristics. Therefore, by tuning the states of the unit, the proposed array allows for dynamic manipulation of the scattering beam without compromising the radiation performance, thereby significantly reducing the in-band monostatic and bistatic RCS. Finally, the reconfigurable units form an 8×8 circularly polarized antenna array. The proposed circularly polarized antenna array demonstrates in-band low scattering characteristics under both x- and y-polarized incidences, along with the capability to adjust the shape of its scattering beam. In addition, the proposed antenna array can maintain good and stable circular polarization performance in different states.

articleTitle: Multilayer and Low-Profile Optically Semi-Transparent Antenna for Conformal Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A low-profile, lightweight, and optically semitransparent multilayer antenna based on stacked patches for conformal applications is presented. The antenna employs multiple layers of patches utilizing the polytetrafluoroethylene film and polyethylene foam for bandwidth enhancement and high level of bending. The antenna is designed for the L-band and tested for the flat case as well as conformed to a cylinder with radius of 200 mm, 160 mm, 80 mm, and 40 mm. The proposed antenna has a bandwidth of 1.172–1.328 GHz (12.5%), and the gain varies from 8.14 dBi to 5.08 dBi for different cases of conforming to a cylinder.

articleTitle: Generating Mode 1/-1 Circularly Polarized Nonvortex OAM Beams Using Uniform Circular Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this paper, uniform circular arrays (UCA) capable of generating non-vortex mode 1/-1 circularly polarized orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams are designed and simulated. The generated OAM beams have the characteristic helical phase front, but the radiation pattern does not have a null at the center in the direction of propagation. This is in contrast to the typical OAM beams, which not only carry the helical phase fronts but also have a null at the center of their radiation patterns. This is achieved by applying the OAM mode 1/-1 excitation phases to the antenna elements and sequentially rotating the antenna elements of the UCA by an amount equal to their excitation phases. Furthermore, it is shown that the rotation and the excitation phases conflate to result in a circularly polarized beam. Several examples of such arrays designed at 17.8 GHz operating frequency are presented via full-wave simulations in the CST Microwave Studio software. Such non-vortex OAM beams could enable high data rate long-range communications by multiplexing several beams.

articleTitle: Time-Frequency Resolution Analysis for Continuous Human Activity Recognition using Radar Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The effect of different time-frequency (TF) resolution values is analyzed in the context of Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using multiple radars distributed in a network. Specifically, different spectrograms computed with various Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) window lengths and Morse wavelet transform are compared as input representation to a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), together with a coherent combination of multiple spectrograms. The study emphasizes the importance of selecting appropriate window sizes for TF analysis and for classification, balancing the observation time with the physical duration of the diverse activities, and also avoiding correlation between different data samples that may compromise the generalization ability of the method. The results employing this coherent sensor fusion demonstrate the efficacy of the investigated method, achieving an F1 score of 0.943 on a challenging public dataset containing 9 activities performed by 15 participants.

articleTitle: Novel C-band Firecone shaped patch antenna design with High Beamwidth and Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper explores a novel design of a microstrip patch antenna with a firecone-shaped design. The unique design has a wide beam width, high gain, and bandwidth efficiency. The main operating frequency range of this antenna is in the 5 to 5.8GHz, the optimal frequency is at 5.2GHz. A wide beamwidth of more than 100 degrees is achieved with a gain of 11 dBi given a patch of dimensions 53 x 54 mm. The antenna is designed and simulated using CST Studio Suite and fabricated on a dual substrate of Rogers RO4350B (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of 3.66 and thickness 0.786mm), and FR-4 (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of 4.4 and thickness of 0.786mm). The main parameters considered during the analysis and simulations are gain, beam width, return loss, and S11 parameters. The fabricated antenna matches the designed simulation and has yielded optimal results.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Millimeter-Wave Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna with Second-Order Bandstop Filtering Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band differentially fed dual-polarized magnetoelectric (ME) dipole with second-order bandstop filtering, covering bands of 24.25–29.5GHz and 37–40GHz. To introduce two transmission zeros, hairpin and coupled λ/4 open-/short-circuited stub resonators are integrated into the ME dipole. This results in a sharp band-edge selectivity without footprint increase. The proposed antenna shows a portto-port isolation of more than 28.3dB. The measured results show lower than –24dB cross-polarization level. The measured peak gains of the single element and 2×2 array are 9.9dBi and 12.2dBi, respectively. The array presents a band rejection of 22.5dB.

articleTitle: Parasitic array loaded with shorting vias on beam steering patch antenna for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this paper, a beam steering patch antenna with two parasitic array elements loaded with shorting vias for sub-6 GHz 5G applications is proposed. Two parasitic elements placed at the upper left and below right of the circular driven patch. The mutual coupling effect between both driven and parasitic has managed to steer the beam. The parasitic elements electrically shorten the ground plane through shorting vias. In simulation, shorting vias is like an artificial switch that connects parasitic element to ground plane to change its effective electrical length hence forming a reflector and director. Based on the condition of the shorting vias either ON/OFF, the proposed antenna is able to steer the main beam in three different directions to ±23° and 0° at the resonant frequency of 3.5 GHz with maximum gain of 7.54 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized SFSS with High Selectivity and High Switching Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this article, a miniaturized switchable FSS (SFSS) with high selectivity and high switching isolation is proposed based on parallel plate capacitor (PPC) structure. PIN diodes are loaded building an asymmetric structure, and makes resonances of different layers misalign, which leads to high switching isolation. Large PPC miniaturizes the SFSS, and reduces Q-factor of reflection resonance to extend the out-of-band suppression range. The proposed SFSS presents high miniaturization, the passband is from 2.18 to 2.81 GHz in OFF state, and the |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| is less than −10 dB from 3.31 to 22.58 GHz. In ON state, |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>| is less than −20 dB from 0 to 22.9 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Isolated Eight-Element Slot MIMO Antennas Based on Current Couplings Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband eight-element linearly-placed MIMO slot antenna array is proposed. By bending the slot antenna L-shaped, the current couplings on the two portions are opposite and cancel out to achieve the first transmission zero. Another transmission zero is reached by adding the short-ended L-shaped branch on the center of the original slot antenna using the same decoupling mechanism. By adjusting the size of the L-shaped slot, the proposed current cancellation scheme can be easily applied to more than two elements in the antenna array. Utilizing the proposed current cancellation method, an eight-element linear slot array is constructed with all the mutual couplings greater than 15 dB from 3.3 to 3.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Electromagnetically Controlled Beam-Steerable mm-wave Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A circular polarized beam-steerable reflectarray antenna with an electromagnetic control mechanism is presented in this communication. The phase reflection of the proposed reflectarray unit elements is altered by physically moving a pin actuator between two positions using electromagnetism. The proposed design is simulated to have an impedance bandwidth of more than 4.8 GHz and a -3 dB gain bandwidth is more than 2.25 GHz. The realized circularly polarized gain is found to be 21.2 dBi at the center frequency of 25 GHz. The antenna can beam-steer in an 85-degree range with a gain drop of less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Automotive Glass Antennas Using Commercial Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of glass antennas for automotive use by conducting field tests in urban and rural areas using a coherent base station scanner. The study compares the glass antennas attached to the vehicle windows with rod antennas installed on the instrumental panel. Measurements of RSRP, SINR, correlation, and the channel capacity are taken, and the results indicate that glass antennas achieve higher channel capacity in rural regions compared to antennas on the instrumental panel. The study concludes that glass antennas offer advantages in terms of channel capacity, especially in rural areas.

articleTitle: Field Measurement on an Extended Pseudo-Scale Model of Air-Shallow Sea Problems at 200 MHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: To solve a difficulty in conductivity-invariant pseudo-scale models or the inability to satisfy the conducting medium condition after scale conversion, we apply a pseudo-scale model that allows conductivity changes before and after scale conversion to the air-sea water two-layer problem and measure field distributions in a tank installed in the laboratory. We construct an experimental system simulating air-seawater problem, and measure the received power distribution from a transmitting antenna with a scale factor of n=200 and a conductivity magnifier of m=2, and compared it with the simulated distribution by using FDTD method for the original model with (n, m) = (1, 1). We also compare the measured distribution for the conductivity-changing pseudo-scale model with (n, m) = (200, 2) with that of the conductivity-invariant pseudo-scale model with (n, m) = (100, 1), and discuss how the reflected waves from the tank wall affect the distribution.

articleTitle: Surface Wave Propagation Enhancement and Control Using Metasurfaces Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel design for a wireless communication system that uses planar surface wave excitation. The design includes a wideband, low-profile quasi-rectangular aperture with a compact Co-planar wave guide surface wave launcher. The study compares surface wave propagation on a reactive plane platform with four different metasurface platforms, and the proposed design enhances high-efficiency surface wave propagation along various meta-surfaces. The system provides a wide bandwidth of 21GHz to 30GHz with low return loss below -10dB for millimeter-wave frequencies between 20 and 30GHz, designed for 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: Axial Ratio and Gain Measurements for Circularly-Polarized Antenna using Two Identical Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: An efficient method of measuring the axial ratio (AR) and realized gain is proposed for circularly-polarized antennas. The setup involves a transmitting-receiving system with two identical antennas and a vector network analyzer. The transmission coefficients of the transmitting-receiving system when the receive antenna is rotated by angle 0° and 90° are sufficient to obtain the AR, the realized gain, and the sense of rotation. A narrowband circular polarized patch antenna is simulated to validate the method over a large AR variation range. The excellent agreement between the simulated and calculated results demonstrates the accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Circularly-polarized Antenna Arrays in Package with Rotated Sequential Feeding Network for Millimeterwave Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper proposes rotated sequential feeding network for circularly-polarized antenna arrays in package to achieve broad 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth. The proposed antenna consists of multiple layers containing radiating patches, quadrature feed, rotated sequential feed, and power supply lines. This multilayer feeding network allows for exciting balanced 90° phase difference to the circular patch antennas with a phase error less than 5° in the target bandwidth. Consequently, the axial ratio bandwidth is improved from 7.1% to 75%, compared to the conventional feeding mechanism. Furthermore, the axial ratio characteristics remain stable for the beam steering operation within the range of θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ≤ 60°.

articleTitle: Development of Jerusalem Cross type Rasorber for Wide-Angle Rasorbing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In recent years, to expand the wireless communication quality, metasurfaces are widely developed. Several kinds of metasurfaces are proposed. One of a unique metasurface is a Rasorber. The rasorber is a structure that acts as an electromagnetic wave absorber at some frequencies, and act as a transmits radio waves at other frequencies, and acts as a reflector at other frequencies. Rasorber can be used to prevent information leakage by attaching it to inside of room windows. However, Rasorber which developed in the past does not have good oblique incident characteristics. In this study, a Rasorber with good oblique incident characteristics was developed. From the results, the developed Rasorber has good oblique incident characteristics comparing with conventional Rasorbers. The Developed Rasorber has same characteristics for incident angle from 0° to 75°.

articleTitle: On the Field Measurement of a Highly Efficient Reflectarray Antenna Using Electromagnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper introduces a measurement on a highly efficient reflectarray antenna using electromagnets. Since the reflectarray antenna under test is electrically large, conventional measurement in an anechoic chamber is not available and field measurement is required. To eliminate the reflection interference from the ground, two approaches are proposed and utilized in the measurement. As a result, by simultaneously applying both methods, the measurement error is improved around 2.5 dB. This work provides another option to measure the reflectarray antenna with comparatively lower cost without significantly sacrificing the percision and accuracy.

articleTitle: Flexible Substrate based D-band End-fire Antenna for 6G application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: We proposed a D-band end-fire array antenna on a flexible substrate for 6G applications. The antenna was designed using full-wave simulation, and experiments were conducted to validate the design. We achieved approximately 15 GHz bandwidth and 12.0 dBi peak realized gain in a four-element array antenna, as measured by the far-field method and a frequency extender of a vector network analyzer.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of LC Materials for Display and Non-display Applications in Ku-Band 6x6 Antenna Array Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This research focuses on the evaluation of LC materials for display and non-display applications in a Ku-Band 6x6 antenna array structure. Conventional LC materials for display applications i.e. Merck E7 were used to compare with the LC materials that have been developed for EM wave applications i.e. Merck GT7-29001 and JNC ZOC-A017XX. In the proposed antenna array, a slotted coupling feeding method was employed. Numerical simulations demonstrate that all LC materials can achieve beam scanning ranges of over ±45 degrees, exhibiting excellent gain and directivity. However, JNC ZOC-A017XX LC materials can achieve a better frequency tunability of over 6.4%.

articleTitle: An RFID-Controlled Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a promising technology to enhance the spectral efficiency of sixth-generation (6G) wireless communications by leveraging their exceptional electromagnetic wave manipulation capabilities. In this paper, we propose an ultra-long-range and nearly-passive radio frequency identification (RFID)-controlled RIS to address the high power consumption and complexity challenges associated with RIS. Our proposed RIS consists of an 8×8 array of unit cells, with each cell integrated with a single pole double throw (SPDT) switch chip enabling 1-bit phase reconfigurability. Simulation and experimental results successfully demonstrate the beam splitting function of the RIS, which can be wirelessly controlled by RFID technology within a range of 21.7m. Additionally, the static power consumption of the system is measured to be only 0.576mW, highlighting its nearly passive nature.

articleTitle: Self-Duplexing Antennas for Wireless and Satellite Applications (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
