abstract: In wireless and satellite applications, the transmit (Tx) and the Receive (Rx) systems always working in different frequency range for enhancing the isolation between the Tx and Rx channels. In this paper, several highly-integrated self-duplexing antennas based on filtering antenna techniques are presented to generate the two isolated channels/ports with a single radiator. Such a co-design approach can not only simplify RF frontend system by getting rid of duplexers but also significantly improving the efficiency. First, the mechanism of a linearly-polarized self-duplexing antenna is introduced, which is followed by our recent research outcomes, including a dual-polarized self-duplexing antenna and a circularly-polarized self-duplexing antennas. Good performance in terms of impedance bandwidths, inter-channel isolation and radiation is achieved. The proposed self-duplexing antenna could be a good candidate for a wide range wireless and satellite applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Modeling in Antenna Array Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: With the fast development in modern wireless communication, the complexity of the modern antenna array design increases rapidly with the increasing element number. Conventional antenna array design methodologies introduce knowledge-guided perceptions and assumptions to achieve highly effective antenna array design, without considering mutual coupling and platform effects. Such effects could worsen beam quality, especially for arrays with small or medium array size. Data-driven methodologies including machine learning-assisted modeling method provide powerful tools to consider those affections within the design procedure. In this article, the machine learning methods are introduced in several scenarios in antenna array designs, including the modeling of active element patterns under mutual coupling, the decoupling performance of defected ground and the base element performance in series-fed antenna array. It can be seen that the introduction of machine learning-assisted modeling could be of great help in antenna array designs.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band and High-Gain Antenna with a Large Frequency Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a compact dual-band and high-gain shared-aperture antenna for sub-6 GHz and K-band application. At the lower band, a Fabry-Perot cavity antenna (FPCA) works as the radiator and a folded reflectarray (FRA) operates at the higher band. To hybridize these two kinds of antennas together and achieve a high aperture reuse efficiency, the unit cell (UC) constituting the upper aperture should be able to partially reflect the incident wave at the lower band and act as the polarization grating (PG) at the higher band; for unit cell constituting the lower aperture, it needs to function as the metal ground at the lower band while twist the polarization of the reflective wave and implement the phase compensation at the higher band. To satisfy the above requirements, two kinds of unit cells are studied, analyzed and used to construct a shared-aperture antenna. The results show that the antenna realizes an effective bandwidth (for reflection coefficient ≤ −10 dB and gain variation ≤ 3 dB) from 5.62 to 5.94 GHz at the lower band, and from 19.5 to 26 GHz at the higher band. The peak gain is 16 dBi and 27.4 dBi at two bands, respectively.

articleTitle: Two-layered High Gain and Wide Bandwidth Metamaterial Antenna for 5G mm-Wave Applications Using Multi-Trial Vector-Based Differential Evolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A two-layered high gain and wide bandwidth metamaterial antenna working at 24 GHz - 30.5 GHz for mm-Wave applications is presented in this paper. To design the antenna we apply a novel evolutionary algorithm, namely the multi-trial vector-based differential evolution (MTDE). The metamaterial antenna has an overall compact size of 12.4 x 12.4 x 8.38 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> including two substrates and the air gap. It is realized with a Rogers Duroid 5880 substrate 0.78 mm thick and a Rogers RO3010 as a superstrate 1.6 mm thick at an optimized distance above the radiation element. The radiation element is composed of a square-cut-at-the-four corners patch antenna. In addition, to enhance the antenna performance, both gain and bandwidth, a metasurface based on periodic metallic mushrooms which surround the radiation element is employed. Interelement distance between the metallic structures, their size and the distance between the two substrates are optimized. Simulated results show a significantly wide bandwidth ranging 24 GHz to 30.5 GHz and a high peak realized gain of 11.76 dB when the MTDE optimizer is applied. These features make the antenna a good candidate for 5G mm-Wave applications.

articleTitle: 100 years history of the Yagi-Uda Antenna : The Yagi-Uda antenna used for television reception and has the history along with the spread of television broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: One hundred years after the birth of the Yagi-Uda antenna, which has made great contributions to television reception, this article introduces the Yagi-Uda antenna along with historical transitions in television broadcasting.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Yagi-Uda Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the advances in reconfigurable Ygai-Uda antenna for smart wireless communications systems. In particularly, it reports the development of planar Yagi-Uda antenna with frequency and pattern reconfiguration. Furthermore, this paper presents a recent design on a circular array of Yagi-Uda monopoles with a full 360° azimuthal beam scanning.

articleTitle: Measurement Results of Broadbanding a Reflectarray Antenna by Controlling Phase Center of Primary Radiator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Reflector array antenna consists of a horn antenna as the primary radiator and a reflector mirror made of planes. The antenna has the disadvantage of narrow bandwidth due to phase errors on the aperture plane at frequencies other than the design frequency. Various studies have been conducted to improve the narrow-bandwidth characteristics, but the gain reduction due to phase error is a major bottleneck in reflector array design. In this study, we investigate the residual aberration, which is considered to be inevitable in the characteristics of reflective array antennas, for wideband reflective array antennas, focusing on the primary radiator in the reflective array antenna. A method to correct the residual aberration by controlling the phase center position of the primary radiator is proposed, and a wideband reflectarray antenna using this method is described and its effectiveness is verified from measurement results.

articleTitle: A Dual-passbands FSS with Wide Angular Stability and High Polarization Stability for 5G and EMC Pulse Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: An excellent frequency selective surface (FSS) with capacitance loading and multi-layer structure is proposed, primarily for application in the sub-6 and shielding. The proposed FSS has two different operational passbands to cover the frequencies located at 3.68 GHz and 5.85 GHz, respectively, which is also a multi-layered unit consisting of three metal layers and two dielectric layers. The unit size is 0.125λ, and the unit profile is 0.075λ, where λ corresponds to the resonance frequency of the first operating band. By adjusting the structural dimensions and parameters, the operating bands can be well-tuned. Simulation results demonstrate favorable polarization stability and angular stability, making it good for pulse shielding.

articleTitle: Multiple People Detection & Localization with Multistatic UWB Radar in Vehicle Cabin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The problem of detection and localization of multiple people using a network of Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) radar nodes in the cabin of a vehicle is addressed in this paper. Specifically, an algorithm for decentralized vital signs detection is proposed, based on the analysis of a novel model for radar signatures of vital signs. Additionally, a centralized association processing block is used to fuse the detections from all radars in the network using a dedicated cost-matrix computation. The performance of the proposed processing pipeline is tested experimentally with a multistatic radar network, and a simulation framework is also developed to evaluate the performance in alternative topologies of the radar network beyond the experiments. It is shown that the detection and localization of humans within the car environment is possible with the proposed processing pipeline, with localization Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 16cm for both single and double target scenarios. Moreover, the distribution of multiple radars and the introduction of bistatic geometries enhance the detection and localization.

articleTitle: FDTD Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering Sheet Using Surface Impedance Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Electromagnetic scattering sheet (EMSS) is a structure which can diffuse an incoming EM field to many different directions. EMSS can be configured with a specific combination of perfectly electric conductor (PEC) and perfectly magnetic conductor (PMC). To analyze the EMSS, collocation of both electric and magnetic fields at the medium surface is required, which is not compatible with the conventional FDTD method. To address this problem, the fast inverse Laplace transform and Prony method is applied to incorporate the surface impedance of an electric conductor with σ = 58×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> S/m to model a PEC while a PMC is modeled by enforcing the magnetic field at the medium surface to be zero. Validation of the PEC modeling is confirmed from 1D simulation results. Scattering cross section of the EMSS is calculated and compared with the result obtained by the method of moments.

articleTitle: Epsilon-Near-Zero (ENZ) Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) metamaterials possess the exotic feature of infinite wavelength, which brings a uniform field distribution while decoupling the space and time. Benefiting from this feature, ENZ antennas have demonstrated promising characteristics, including geometrical flexibility and beam synthesizing ability. In this paper, we have overviewed the recent development on ENZ antennas, with theoretical analysis and demonstration on the key features. Firstly, a geometrical-flexible antenna design is showcased, with a fixed resonant frequency despite being translated into different topologies. Then, an antenna array with beam synthesizing technique is displayed, with arbitrarily reconfigurable radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Restoration Strategies for the Radiation Pattern of a 5G mmWave 1×4 Antenna Array Embedded in a Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The integration of a 5G mmWave 1×4 antenna array into an actual smartphone presents substantial challenges for antenna engineers. This is notably reflected in the considerable impact on various antenna performance metrics, including radiation patterns, gain, efficiency, impedance matching, isolation, and more. Despite these challenges, the existing literature lacks in-depth exploration of restoration strategies or solutions. This paper explores the implications of this scenario, offering a solution to address these challenges, with a particular focus on restoring radiation patterns and gain.

articleTitle: Study on Characteristics of SIW Bandpass-Filter Loaded with Full and Reduced Size of Artificial Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this paper, a study on the characteristics of a substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW) bandpass-filter (BPF) loaded with artificial dielectric material (ADM) is investigated through simulation and experimental measurement. The dimensions of proposed SIW BPF take 66 mm length, 40 mm width, and 3.2 mm thickness, with FR4 Epoxy materials used as the dielectric substrate. The investigation result indicates that the characteristics of SIW BPF loaded with reduced-size of ADM is almost similar to the one with full-size of ADM. This is beneficial to reduce the need of ADM size while maintaining the characteristics of SIW BPF.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Lens Horn Antenna in the 300 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper describes the results of designing and evaluating prototype 30 dBi and 47 dBi lens horn antennas with WR-3.4 as input/output interface and conical horn antenna as primary radiator. The 30 dBi lens horn antenna showed good agreement between the antenna gain measured by the 3-antenna method at 1 m, which is the far field region, and the calculation results, confirming the correctness of the lens design method. For the 47 dBi lens horn antenna, the antenna gains measured by the comparative method at 1 m and 2 m in the near field region was compared with the calculated antenna gain in the near field region.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Proximity Coupled Cavity-less Magneto-electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The modern communication system imposes high specification antennas. Magento-electric dipole antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth, high gain and unidirectional pattern. This work presents a new low-profile magneto-electric dipole which is proximity-fed. The antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth of 45% and a high gain of 9.8 dBi with 1.7 dB in-band variation.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Low-Permittivity Lens for Sub-THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a low-permittivity (LP) extended hemispherical lens antenna with dual-layer matching sections for sub-terahertz (sub-THz) applications at 220–330GHz. The matching layers between the source and the lens work as quarter-wavelength transformers whose main role is to provide a smooth transition from high to low permittivity. A rectangular waveguide feed is used to illuminate the lens. The analysis is done by attaching the waveguide to the lens surface and by introducing an air gap between them. The results show that this air gap improves impedance matching and radiation performance across the operating band.

articleTitle: Low-Cost FR-4 Metasurface-Enhanced Microstrip Patch Antenna Array for Wideband 5G millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost metasurface (MTS)-enhanced microstrip patch antenna (MPA) array for wideband 5G mmWave applications. The MTS and MPA are fabricated using FR-4 PCB processes, ensuring affordability and accessibility. The designed MTS mitigates the high loss of FR-4 substrate and improves performance. Results show a |S11| <=-10 dB bandwidth of 32.3% (24.1-33.4 GHz) and a maximum gain of 19.7 dBi. Compared to an MPA array without the MTS, the MTS-enhanced antenna achieves an 8 dB gain improvement (11.7 dBi). This design offers an economical solution for enhancing mmWave communication systems, facilitating the cost-effective deployment of 5G technology.

articleTitle: A Dual-band MIMO Antenna for Wi-Fi 6E / 7 System in a Small Base Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this article, a 6 × 6 MIMO patch antenna design is proposed for application in the dual-band Wi-Fi 6E / 7 system. This antenna model covers the Wi-Fi 6E / 7 frequency bands of 2.38-2.44 GHz and 4.9-7.125 GHz. And, the proposed antenna provides measured peak gains and antenna efficiencies close to 6.4 / 10 / 8.6 dBi and 75 / 80 / 70 % across the 2.45 / 5.5 / 6.5 GHz operating bands, respectively. Also, the measured envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is less than 0.3 across the operating bands for the MIMO patch antennas.

articleTitle: Development of Low-Loss and Low-Cost Air-Filled Transmission Lines based on Advanced Glass Wafer Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: To solve the problem of high dielectric loss of glass in mm-W/THz bands, we proposed two types of low-cost and low-loss air-filled transmission lines based on advanced glass wafer packaging. They are the air-filled double-sided gap waveguide (DS-GWG) and post-wall waveguide (PWWG). It is verified that those two solutions have excellent transmission performance in the mm-W band. The low-loss and low-cost characteristics can also be realized in the THz band because of the high-precision glass wafer packaging.

articleTitle: A Dual-band, Dual-polarized, Single-layer-fed Millimeter-wave Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fully Compatible with PCB Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This work presents a new design of dual-band dual-polarized dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) in the millimeter-wave (mmw) band. The DRA element is excited by a single-layered scheme, i.e. a probe-fed patch underneath it. A pin is loaded in the center of the DRA element in order to elaborate the concerned DR modes. Contributed by the patch and DR, the desired dual-band operation is achieved by virtue of the multiple resonate modes that elaborated in the concerned frequency bands. The resulting antenna element is compact (0.32λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>× 0.32λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>) and low-profile (0.11λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>) with promising performance (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the free-space wavelength at the starting frequency).

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Low-profile Folded Dipole Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The gain of a low-profile antenna can be improved by dielectric layer. This paper presents a low-profile and compact folded dipole antenna array with a dielectric layer to improve the gain. The gain of 9.05 dBi is obtained with dielectric layer under the low-profile folded dipole antenna array.

articleTitle: Four-port printed MIMO Dipole Antennas at Wi-Fi 6E/7 Bands for Wireless Modem Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A design of four-port MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) dipole antennas at Wi-Fi 6E/7 bands (2.4-2.484 GHz, 5.15 – 7.125 GHz) for wireless modem applications is proposed. The printed dipole is printed on an FR4 substrate with a dielectric constant of 4.4, a thickness of 1.6 mm and a loss tangent of 0.0245. Positioned around the base plate, four printed dipole antennas are employed. The dipole antenna consists of a two-arm dipole and a parasitic C-shaped strip. The dipole is excited by a mini-cable. The two-arm dipole antenna is responsible for exciting Wi-Fi 6E/7 bands and enhancing low-frequency matching by using a parasitic C-shaped strip around the two-arm dipole. The dipole antenna with a reflector improves antenna gain and directivity. The distance between the dipole antenna and the reflector is 15.625mm. The overall dimensions of the design are 123.2 mm x 81.6 mm x 71.6 mm. From the measured results, The S parameters within the frequency bands are all lower than -10dB, and the measured isolation parameters are all lower than -15dB. The simulated gain falls within the range of 3.6 – 4dBi for low frequencies and 4.1 – 6.4dBi for high frequencies. The design exhibits good performances is good for wireless modem applications at the Wi-Fi 6E/7 bands.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Dual-Band Transparent Antenna for WLAN Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a cost-effective dual-band transparent antenna designed for WLAN communications, operating at 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz. Utilizing a low-cost 0.8-mm acrylic sheet substrate and 40-mesh copper wire conductor, the antenna, inspired by a monopole design, employs an F-shaped radiating patch fed by a microstrip transmission line. Simulated and measured results show strong agreement, revealing an impedance bandwidth of 240 MHz (2.26 – 2.50 GHz) and 500 MHz (4.96 – 5.46 GHz). With maximum gains of 2.1 dBi and 4 dBi, the antenna provides an omnidirectional pattern at lower frequencies and a bidirectional pattern at higher frequencies.

articleTitle: Prior Knowledge-Guided Deep Learning Algorithms for Metantenna Design (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents the recent advances in deeplearning (DL)-enabled methods for metacell and metalens design. On one hand, metamaterials or metasurfaces have been new opportunities for innovative antenna (metantennas) designs by increasing the degrees of freedom (DoF) in design through introducing new physical properties in antenna design. On the other hand, the increased DoF significantly increases the complexity of design procedure, demanding for new design methods. Prior-knowledge-guided deep-learning-enabled (PK-DL) synthesis method has been then proposed to alleviate this challenge. Prior knowledge is introduced into the conditional deep convolutional generative adversarial networks (cDCGAN) algorithm to guide and speed up the proposed synthesis method. Then, two case studies are presented. The PK-DL synthesis method is first utilized to break the phaseshift limit up to 330 degrees from 308 degrees in existing techniques and improve the 1-dB gain bandwidth of metalens antennas by 52%. Secondly, both amplitude and phase responses of metacells are simultaneously synthesized in a single three-layered metasurface for a metalens antenna, realizing the sidelobe level suppression more than 30 dB. The latest progress demonstrates that the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to metantenna design and AI technologies provide a new opportunity in synthesizing metantennas with outstanding performances and multiple functions.
